description: Mido and the forest exit stop blocking Link, as child or adult
label: Open Forest

description: The Kakariko gate guard has already seen Zelda's letter, so the Death Mountain trail is open from the start
label: Open Kakariko Gate

description: Link starts having met Zelda, with her letter in hand, and Talon and Malon back at Lon Lon Ranch. Her letter's check holds the letter. Impa's check comes at the start (Zelda's Lullaby, unless Songs are shuffled), and Malon's does too when NPC gifts are shuffled. Zelda's Letter and the Weird Egg have been removed from the pool
label: Met Zelda

description: With Open, the Door of Time stands open from the start, so Link can grow up without the stones or the Song of Time. Zelda and Impa stay until he's met them. He skips Rauru, whose gift comes at the start, and can put the sword back any time. With Closed, it opens as in the game: once Link has met Zelda, brought the three stones to her scene at the moat, and plays the Song of Time on the Ocarina of Time
label: Door of Time

description: Jabu-Jabu's mouth is open, so child Link walks in without giving him a fish
label: Jabu-Jabu Open

description: The waterfall at the end of Zora's River already stands split, so Link reaches Zora's Domain without Zelda's Lullaby
label: Zora's River Waterfall Open

description: The debris in front of the Deku Tree's mouth is gone, so adult Link walks in and out
label: Adult Deku Tree

description: How the four carpenters in the Gerudo Fortress start. With Normal, Link frees all four, as in the game. With Fast, freeing any one frees all four and earns the membership card, and the other thieves still guard their cells. With Freed, all four are free from the start, with the membership card in hand, the guards standing down and the valley bridge up. Their thieves still stand, and beating one opens her cell without freeing anyone twice
label: Gerudo Fortress

description: What people hand over becomes a check: their gifts, minigame prizes, the House of Skulltula's rewards and the Great Fairies' upgrades
label: NPC Gifts

description: Twelve songs become checks, given without the lesson: Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Saria's Song, the Sun's Song, the Song of Time, the Song of Storms and Sheik's six. The Scarecrow's Song stays where it is
label: Songs

description: With NPC gifts on, the House of Skulltula's reward for all 100 tokens is a check too. Off, it pays its Gold Rupee as always, and logic never sends Link for all 100
label: 100-Token Reward

description: Each trade on the way to Biggoron's sword becomes a check, from Anju's Pocket Egg to Biggoron's Claim Check, and the ten trade items join the pool. Showing an item to the one who wants it gives that check, whatever order Link finds them in. Grog or Fado waits at the stump by which item Link holds. The Pocket Cucco still hatches from the egg
label: Adult Trade Quest

description: People who sell one thing sell a check once, for the price of the thing: Medigoron's Giant's Knife, the carpet merchant's Bombchus, and the bean seller's first bean. Bombchus and beans stay on sale after that
label: Merchants

description: The pedestal holds an item from the pool, and the Master Sword can turn up anywhere. Pulling or returning the sword still travels through time without it. Adult Link without it has no sword
label: Master Sword

description: Shelf slots in the eight shops sell checks, each once, at a random price. Prices over 99 rupees need a bigger wallet in logic
label: Shopsanity

description: How many slots of each shop sell a check with Shopsanity on. The rest sell what they always did
label: Shop Slots

description: The fourteen heart pieces lying out in the world are checks. One that holds something else shows it, spinning where the piece was
label: Freestanding Heart Pieces

description: Each of the eight cows gives a check once, for Epona's Song. After that it gives milk, which still needs a bottle
label: Cows

description: Each of the 100 Gold Skulltulas drops a check when killed. A token for each goes in the pool, so the House of Skulltula still counts them. Logic wants the Boomerang or Hookshot for every one
label: Gold Skulltulas

description: The heart container each of the eight bosses leaves behind is a check
label: Boss Heart Containers

description: The Spiritual Stones and five medallions become checks, given by the scene after each boss. Light stays with Rauru
label: Dungeon Rewards

description: Each dungeon's map and compass turn up at random checks anywhere, and mark their own dungeon wherever Link finds them. Keys stay where they are
label: Maps and Compasses

description: With Start, Link holds every dungeon's small keys and boss key from the start. The 43 chests that held a key become checks. With Start each brings a Red Rupee to the pool. The two keys lying in the open stay where they are
label: Keys

description: With Start, Link holds the four Gerudo Fortress keys from the start, so every cell opens whatever the thieves drop. With Keysanity, each key turns up at a random check, anywhere. Either way, the four keys the thieves carry become checks
label: Fortress Keys

description: What caps the Bombchus Link holds. The bomb bag's, as in the game. Their own cap of 40, so they open the same checks bombs do without waiting on the bag.
label: Bombchus

description: Turns on every skip below. Cutscenes that give an item, set a flag or move Link still play
label: Skip All Cutscenes

description: All small makes every chest a small one, which opens without the big chest's long animation. What a chest holds doesn't change
label: Chest Size

description: Navi never stops Link to talk on her own: the Lost Woods warning, dungeon and quest tips, and reminders. Hints you ask her for still work
label: Quiet Navi

description: Link runs half again as fast while he wears the Bunny Hood
label: Bunny Hood Speed

description: Child and adult Link can each wield every one-handed sword and every shield, and logic expects them to. Biggoron's Sword and the Giant's Knife stay adult Link's, and only he can aim the Mirror Shield at light
label: One-Handed Swords and Shields for Both Ages
